The US PCE inflation and GDP releases scheduled for September 30, 2026 are official BEA calendar events, not results already announced. At 8:30 a.m. EDT, BEA plans to publish August personal income and outlays—including the monthly PCE price indexes—and the third estimate of second-quarter GDP alongside a major annual update.

R

By Reddy News Desk
Published 26 September 2026, 10:55 AM IST · 12 min read [...] Yes—two major US economic releases are officially scheduled for Wednesday, September 30, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. EDT. The US Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) calendar lists Personal Income and Outlays for August 2026, which contains the monthly Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price indexes, and a separate second-quarter GDP package headed by GDP (Third Estimate). The calendar is the authoritative confirmation that the events are scheduled; as of this draft’s September 26 verification, the [...] State PCE in the GDP package should not be confused with the national monthly PCE price index. The calendar describes it as State PCE for 2025, meaning a state-level annual spending release. The national price indexes that readers generally mean by ‘PCE inflation’ are part of the August personal-income and outlays report. Keeping those labels separate will help prevent a headline about state spending from being mistaken for the August national inflation result.
